summary: Iteration 9 — Push Notifications (Web Push + VAPID), Photo Uploads (Emergent Object Storage), APScheduler cron worker. Backend: 16/16 pytest pass including round-trip upload→GET→delete→404, fake-endpoint push (returns sent>=0 cleanly), cron sweep transition checkin scheduled→alerted. Frontend smoke: /notifications shows 'Permission blocked' state correctly (headless Chrome has no notification permission), /photos shows MAIN badge + 'Choose photo' file input + 2 photos with trash icons, /profile shows photos-link AND notifications-link entry points. Backend logs show no stack traces; 'Scheduler started' + 'Emergent object storage initialized' both present at startup.

minor.issue: PostDateCheckin.match_id is typed as `str` (non-Optional) — passing match_id=null gets a 422 with pydantic v2 'string_type' error. Either make it Optional[str] = None (current schema in code doesn't allow null) or document the requirement. Looking at server.py PostDateCheckin model — match_id field doesn't accept None. If the safety check-in should be allowed without a match (general 'safety walk home' use-case), make this Optional.
Endpoint takes a JSON body via `payload: dict` — works, but loses pydantic validation. Could be tightened to a typed model (DeletePhotoPayload{url:str}). Cosmetic.

Comment says 'Allow unauthenticated GET for now to keep tags simple; can tighten later' — anyone with a path can read any non-deleted file. For a dating app where profile photos are semi-public, OK; but the path uses uuid which is unguessable. Worth documenting that paths are treated as capability tokens.

Fake/dead endpoints generate pywebpush ERROR log entries (one per fake sub). These look noisy. Auto-deactivation on 410/404 works, but transient errors (e.g. bad headers like our test's fake p256dh) log at ERROR — consider downgrading to WARNING for non-410 push failures.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py now 3557 lines — Batch D added another ~330 lines on top. Router split is now urgent. Suggested modules: routers/push.py, routers/files.py, services/storage.py, services/scheduler.py.

init_storage() caches storage_key in a module-level dict `_storage_key_cache` with no TTL — if Emergent storage rotates keys, only 401/403 path triggers refresh. Add a max-age (e.g. 12h) + force-refresh on a timer to avoid first-failure cost on key expiry mid-traffic.

put_object_sync/get_object_sync use blocking `requests` inside asyncio.to_thread — fine, but no retry/backoff for transient 5xx from object store; a single 502 from storage propagates as 502 to the client.

GET /api/files/{path:path} accepts auth via ?auth= query param AND allows fully unauthenticated GET (commented as 'for now'). Token-in-query leaks into web server logs and is generally an anti-pattern. Either fully open public-photo bucket or require Bearer header.

push_notify_user iterates subs sequentially in asyncio.to_thread per webpush call — for a fan-out push (Monday weekly nudge to up to 5000 users), this would be slow. Batch with asyncio.gather and a semaphore.
_scheduled_new_week sends push to up to 5000 users in a single Monday-9am-UTC job with NO concurrency limit and NO backoff — could thundering-herd. Add chunking + asyncio.Semaphore(20).

DELETE /api/profile/photo only soft-deletes (sets is_deleted=True) — never purges from object storage. For GDPR/right-to-be-forgotten, add a TTL background job to actually call object-storage DELETE after N days.

Photo path generation: f'{APP_NAME}/photos/{user_id}/{uuid4}.{ext}' — predictable enough that knowing user_id + brute-forcing uuid4 ext is computationally infeasible BUT enumerating all photos of a user is also impossible. OK.
Push subscription doc still keeps `active=False` after 410 — never purged. Add a TTL index or periodic cleanup so dead subs don't accumulate forever.
VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY is in /app/backend/.env in plaintext — that's standard for self-hosted, but for prod multi-replica, plan to move to a secrets manager.
seed_data_creation: All tests are self-cleaning: push subscriptions inserted with fake endpoint are deleted in finally / via unsubscribe; uploaded test PNG is deleted via DELETE /api/profile/photo and user.photos[] is restored from pymongo snapshot; post_date_checkins inserted/created for cron tests are delete_many'd in finally. No persistent test data left.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iteration9.py -v` (~7s, no LLM). Emergent Object Storage IS REAL — uses EMERGENT_LLM_KEY → init_storage() returns a session storage_key cached in _storage_key_cache (in-process). VAPID keys are real in backend/.env. Scheduler: AsyncIOScheduler (in-process, single worker) runs post_date_sweep every 5min and weekly_challenge_push Mon 09:00 UTC. The owner-triggered POST /api/safety/run-post-date-alerts calls the same _sweep_post_date_alerts(user_id_filter=user_id). To trigger an 'alerted' transition reliably: (1) POST a checkin (requires emergency_contact_email AND a real match_id — match_id field is NON-optional in pydantic schema), (2) pymongo-update auto_notify_at to past, (3) POST /api/safety/run-post-date-alerts. demo1 has 2 photos in production state; if you upload via tests, ALWAYS snapshot+restore user.photos[] in finally. Active push subscriptions for demo1/demo2 are cleaned up by tests.
rca_of_the_issue: No bugs found in iteration 9. All 16 tests + 3 frontend routes + 2 profile entry points green. Only minor/cosmetic enhancements suggested (PostDateCheckin.match_id should accept None; push error log levels; URL-token-via-query anti-pattern; soft-delete TTL purge).
